findings.text: blocking: _selected_fields (reckon/crew/query.py:133) returns COMMON_RUN_FIELDS + requested when fields is passed, and that tuple is handed to _compact_row as selected_fields (query.py:710,713 -> 785,815), whose row is {field: complete[field] for field in selected_fields} at query.py:547. So a run row built for fields=['section'] carries only run_id, node, plan, section (plus member) — it does not carry classification, session_id or resumable. The view's own filters read exactly those keys: _matches (query.py:622-639) compares row.get('classification')/row.get('session_id') as strings and row.get('resumable') by identity, and row.get on an absent key returns None, so str(None or '') != 'blocked' and None is not False both drop the row. Reproduced by reading the commit at the reviewed head: crew(view='runs', fields=['section'], classification='blocked') now answers count:0 where the base commit answered the matching rows, because on the base _selected_fields always returned DEFAULT_RUN_FIELDS (query.py:20-41), which carries all three keys. Same for the session= and resumable= filters. Narrowing belongs in the final projection at query.py:872, after the filters have run, not in the row build.

blocking: directory() projects coordinator['runs'] (reckon/crew/directory.py:214) and unowned_runs (directory.py:217) with two separate project_run_rows calls, and project_run_rows builds its accepted vocabulary from the rows it is handed for that call (query.py:255-259: carried = COMMON_RUN_FIELDS, then update(row) for each row in that one list). When either list is empty the vocabulary collapses to COMMON_RUN_FIELDS, so a field the view does have is refused. A project whose runs all carry a session has an empty unowned_runs, so crew(view='directory', fields=['phase']) raises RunQueryError('unknown directory fields 'phase'; directory fields are node, plan, run_id, section'), which serve_crew_view converts to ok:false at mcp_views.py:3815. Before this change directory() took no fields argument at all (serve_crew_view called crew_directory(project, run_id=run_id, node_id=node)), so the field was accepted and ignored; it now fails the whole view. The accepted vocabulary must be the view's, not the list's.

blocking: obligations() projects 'obligations' (reckon/crew/obligations.py:1383-1385) and 'acknowledged' (obligations.py:1386-1388) through two separate project_run_rows calls, and each call recomputes the accepted vocabulary from its own list (query.py:255-259). acknowledged is empty in the ordinary case — a coordinator with nothing acknowledged — so crew(view='obligations', fields=['kind','age_seconds']) raises RunQueryError('unknown obligations fields 'kind''), the duty rows are lost, and serve_crew_view answers ok:false. The base commit had no fields parameter on obligations() (the call was obligations_module.obligations(project, session)), so this is a regression of the newly wired parameter rather than a pre-existing one. Same root cause as the directory finding: the vocabulary must be the view's field set, not what one list happens to carry.

The reviewed head e0d7e097ed is one commit past the gated 81aa5716c and touches only the evidence fragment, so the code at the head is the code the gate ran.

JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/query.py:872 does route the runs rows through project_run_rows last so all four views share one projection and name the section, but the routing regresses the runs view's own filters (query.py:133) and the projection refuses fields the obligations and directory views do carry (obligations.py:1386, directory.py:217).

JUSTIFICATION durability: the added assertions are independent of the values under test (tests/test_a_row_is_compact_and_names_its_section.py:193 and :237 compare against the literal '§4' while the fixture dispatches 's4'; :369 compares against the literal 'done' while the containing plan reads active), but no committed assertion covers any of the three blocking defects below.
SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: the added names (project_run_rows, run_section_index, dependency_row_state, COMMON_RUN_FIELDS, _canonical_section) are mechanism names in the surrounding docstring idiom of reckon/crew/query.py:183-195, and no plan, sprint, ticket or version identifier appears in the changed source, symbols, comments or the test file.
SCORE reuse: 18
JUSTIFICATION reuse: reckon/crew/query.py:333 delegates project_live_rows' whole-row projection to the new projection instead of keeping a second one, and reckon/roadmap.py:621 gathers the section-state rule that roadmap.py:1368 and mcp.py:1722 each held inline; a capability search over reckon/ for another row projection or dependency-state owner found none — reckon/_schema.py:717 resolve_plan_ref builds the same row shape but answers plan-level refs where the plan status is the correct answer, so it is not a fork of this capability.
FINDING reckon/crew/query.py:133 blocking: _selected_fields now narrows the field set handed to _compact_row (query.py:710,713 -> 785,815), and _compact_row emits only the selected keys (query.py:547), so a row built for fields=['section'] carries no classification, session_id or resumable; the view's own filters read those three (query.py:622-639) with row.get, so crew(view='runs', fields=['section'], classification='blocked') and the session= and resumable= equivalents return an empty row list where the base commit returned the matching rows.
FINDING reckon/crew/directory.py:217 blocking: directory() projects coordinator runs and unowned_runs in two separate project_run_rows calls, and project_run_rows computes the accepted vocabulary from the rows of one call (query.py:255-259), so an empty unowned_runs collapses it to COMMON_RUN_FIELDS and refuses a directory field the view does have — crew(view='directory', fields=['phase']) fails rather than narrowing the rows, where before this change the parameter was accepted and ignored.
FINDING reckon/crew/obligations.py:1386 blocking: same defect on obligations() — 'obligations' and 'acknowledged' are projected separately, so the ordinary case of nothing acknowledged makes crew(view='obligations', fields=['kind','age_seconds']) raise RunQueryError and lose the duty rows, a regression of the newly wired fields parameter.
